plan.contextChunk: This figure contains four sub-panels (a through d) showing the different matrix representations used to encode a graph for graph neural networks. Panel a) depicts a 6-node undirected graph with nodes labeled 1 through 6, connected by edges whose identities are marked by the pair of endpoint node labels (e.g., ‘1\3’, ‘1\4’, ‘2\3’, ‘3\4’, ‘3\6’, ‘4\5’, ‘5\6’). Panel b) shows the adjacency matrix A (N × N), a square binary matrix encoding which pairs of nodes are connected by edges. Panel c) shows the node feature matrix X (D × N), in which each column stores the D-dimensional feature vector associated with one of the N nodes. Panel d) shows the edge feature matrix E (Dᴷ × E), in which each column stores the Dᴷ-dimensional feature vector associated with one of the E edges, with edges ordered to match the labeled pairs in panel a). Labels for each matrix include its name, symbol, and dimensions. This figure introduces the three standard data structures—adjacency matrix, node feature matrix, and edge feature matrix—that together fully represent a graph with node and edge attributes in a deep learning context.

interactionPlan.concept: To process a graph with a neural network, its structure and attributes must be extracted into separate matrices: one for topology (A), one for node features (X), and one for edge features (E).
elements: Panel labels 'a)', 'b)', 'c)', and 'd)'
6 nodes labeled 1 through 6, drawn as circles with brown outlines
7 undirected edges connecting node pairs: (1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (3,4), (3,6), (4,5), (5,6)
Node feature vectors (panel a): 5-element vertical stacks of brown-shaded squares adjacent to each node
Edge feature vectors (panel a): 4-element vertical stacks of teal-shaded squares adjacent to each edge
Text 'Adjacency matrix, A' and dimension 'N x N' (panel b)
6x6 Adjacency matrix grid A, with row and column labels 1-6 and filled cells at connected (i,j) pairs
Text 'Node data, X' and dimension 'D x N' (panel c)
5x6 Node data matrix grid X, with column labels 1-6 and cells filled with various brown shades
Text 'Edge data, E' and dimension 'D_E x E' (panel d)
4x7 Edge data matrix grid E, with stacked column labels for node pairs (1/3, 1/4, 2/3, 3/4, 3/6, 4/5, 5/6) and cells filled with various teal shades

interactions.label: Focus panel
interactions.teaches: Separating the visual graph into distinct mathematical representations isolates topology from attributes.
Clicking a node reveals its column in X and its row/column in A; clicking an edge reveals its column in E and its specific entries in A.

demo_steps.title: The Visual Graph
demo_steps.narration: A graph contains nodes and edges, often with data attributes attached to both (shown here as stacked colored squares).

demo_steps.title: Topology: Adjacency Matrix
demo_steps.narration: The N x N Adjacency matrix (A) encodes pure structure. A filled cell at (i, j) indicates an edge between node i and node j. Because the graph is undirected, the matrix is symmetric.

demo_steps.title: Attributes: Node Data
demo_steps.narration: The node attributes are packed into a D x N matrix (X). Each column represents the D-dimensional feature vector for a single node.

demo_steps.title: Attributes: Edge Data
demo_steps.narration: Similarly, edge attributes are packed into a D_E x E matrix (E). Each column represents the feature vector for a single edge, matching the order of edges in the graph.

demo_steps.title: Explore the Mappings
demo_steps.narration: With all panels visible, click any node or edge in the graph diagram to instantly highlight its corresponding data across the three matrices.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Graph neural networks require disentangling a graph into separate matrix representations for topology (A), node attributes (X), and edge attributes (E) so they can be processed by standard linear algebra operations.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Maintain strict color coding: brown hues for node features (in the graph and matrix X), teal hues for edge features (in the graph and matrix E), and dark slate for adjacency filled cells. In matrix E, stack the edge endpoint labels vertically (e.g., '1' directly over '3') above each column. In panel (a), float the feature vector stacks near their respective nodes or edges so the visual association is clear.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click a node (1–6) in the graph diagram to highlight its row and column in the adjacency matrix A and its column in the node data matrix X
- Click an edge between two nodes to highlight the corresponding entry in the edge data matrix E and the two nodes it connects
- Toggle between panels a–d to compare the visual graph, the N×N adjacency matrix, the D×N node data, and the D_E×E edge data representations

discrepancies: The default presentation state heavily dims panels (b), (c), and (d), violating the requirement that the initial view serve as a fully visible drop-in replacement for the static source image
The titles for matrices X and E ('Node data, X' and 'Edge data, E') are written on a single line, whereas the source figure splits them across two lines
The colors used for the data squares are slightly darker and more muted than the pastel shades in the original figure
evaluation.notes: An exceptional interactive translation of the source figure. The bidirectional click-to-highlight interaction perfectly reinforces the mapping between the visual graph and its matrix representations, though the initial step in the narration should leave all panels fully visible.
action_items: Change the `panelFocus` of the first object in `demoSteps` to 'All Panels' so the initial state renders the full figure without dimming panels b, c, and d.
Split the matrix titles in panels c and d onto two lines (e.g., 'Node\ndata, X') to match the text layout of the source figure.
